text.p: France said on Friday it had nothing to do with French mercenaries reported to be backing a government counter-offensive in Zaire and was not giving any military aid to the Kinshasa government.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said there were only five French military staff in the central African country -- the embassy's defence attache and four security guards.

"If it were verified that French nationals were working as mercenaries in Zaire in a private capacity, such activities could only be condemned in the clearest way as they do not correspond in any way to French policy," he told a news briefing.

The left-wing French daily Liberation said on Friday some 280 European soldiers of fortune, including several French nationals, had gathered in east Zaire under the command of a veteran Belgian mercenary.

In a report from Kisangani, it said there were 16 Frenchmen in the mercenary commander's staff of 19. It said the bulk of the force was in Watsa, some 700 km from Kisangani, and included many Serbs and Croats as well as others from Russia, Poland, France, Belgium and Italy.
France has previously denied any connection with, or knowledge of a mercenary force in Zaire.
Rummelhardt said France had no military cooperation with Zaire and scrupulously respected a European Union embargo on supplies of weapons to the region.
He said Paris wanted the crisis in the Great Lakes region solved with respect for the states' territorial integrity and called for dialogue and negotiation.
Kinshasa said on Thursday its army had launched its promised counter-offensive against Rwanda-backed rebels who have seized a swathe of east Zaire.
